baslik: One Faulty Sensor Kept Pushing the Nose Down
sonuc: dove into the Java Sea minutes after take-off
tetik: a faulty angle-of-attack sensor feeding flight-control software
mekanizma: MCAS repeatedly trimming the nose down based on a single erroneous sensor
ders: MCAS was redesigned to use two sensors and act only once
yanilgi: The pilots weren't fighting a mystery failure they could simply switch off. Most had never been told the MCAS system existed.
tartisma: The system relied on one sensor on a jet that had two. Why would a design ignore its own redundancy?
basliklar: Why Lion Air Flight 610 Crashed
The Software That Fought the Pilots
soru: Would you know to switch it off?
sahneler: Minutes after take-off, a new Boeing 737 MAX dove into the Java Sea.
All one hundred eighty nine people aboard were killed.
A sensor measuring the wing's angle had failed.
Flight software trusted it and pushed the nose down.
The pilots pulled it back up, over and over.
The software kept activating again.
Most pilots hadn't been told the system existed.
It was redesigned to use two sensors and act only once.

baslik: Burning Insulation Brought Down Swissair 111
sonuc: crashed into the Atlantic after a cockpit fire
tetik: arcing wires above the cockpit ceiling
mekanizma: electrical arcing igniting flammable insulation blankets in the ceiling
ders: flammable insulation blankets were replaced across airliner fleets
yanilgi: The smell of smoke seemed minor at first. The real fire was hidden above the ceiling, spreading along the insulation.
tartisma: The crew prepared to dump fuel before landing. Should a fire always mean landing immediately?
basliklar: Why Swissair Flight 111 Crashed
The Hidden Fire Above the Cockpit
soru: Land now, or dump fuel first?
sahneler: An airliner crashed into the Atlantic off Nova Scotia.
It had caught fire in flight, and all two hundred twenty nine aboard were killed.
The crew smelled smoke in the cockpit.
The fire was hidden above the ceiling.
Arcing wires had ignited the insulation blankets there.
The fire spread unseen and knocked out systems one by one.
The jet went down before it could land.
Flammable insulation was replaced across airliner fleets.

baslik: The Autothrottle Everyone Thought Was Holding Speed
sonuc: hit the seawall short of the runway in San Francisco
tetik: an autothrottle left in a mode that did not hold speed
mekanizma: unintended autothrottle mode on a visual approach, letting airspeed decay unnoticed
ders: training on automation modes and manual approaches was strengthened
yanilgi: The engines were working. The crew believed the automation was holding speed when it wasn't.
tartisma: Highly automated jets can make manual flying rare. How do pilots stay sharp when automation does most of the work?
basliklar: Why Asiana Flight 214 Crashed Short of the Runway
When Pilots Trusted the Wrong Automation Mode
sahneler: A Boeing 777 slammed into the seawall at San Francisco airport.
Its tail broke off, and three people were killed.
The approach had been too slow and too low.
The crew believed the autothrottle was holding speed.
It had been left in a mode that didn't.
The airspeed kept falling, and nobody noticed in time.
The go-around came seconds too late.
Training on automation modes was strengthened afterward.

baslik: The Jet That Took Off From the Wrong Runway
sonuc: crashed after taking off from a runway far too short
tetik: a turn onto the wrong runway in the dark
mekanizma: take-off from a short, unlit general-aviation runway instead of the assigned runway
ders: runway-confirmation procedures and cockpit moving-map displays were promoted
yanilgi: The jet had no mechanical fault. It was on the wrong runway, too short for a loaded airliner.
tartisma: Only one controller was on duty and was busy with other tasks. How much should one person be expected to catch?
basliklar: Why Comair Flight 5191 Crashed
The Wrong Runway in the Dark
sahneler: Before dawn, a regional jet ran off the end of a runway in Kentucky.
It crashed into trees, and forty nine people were killed.
It had lined up on the wrong runway.
That runway was short and unlit.
Construction had changed the usual taxi route.
Neither pilot noticed the heading didn't match.
The jet couldn't lift off in time.
Runway-confirmation checks were strengthened afterward.

baslik: Ice That Formed Behind the De-Icing Boots
sonuc: rolled over and crashed while holding in freezing rain
tetik: a ridge of ice forming behind the wing's de-icing boots
mekanizma: supercooled large droplets forming ice beyond the protected area, disturbing airflow over the ailerons
ders: icing certification was expanded to cover large supercooled droplets
yanilgi: The de-icing boots worked. The ice formed just behind them, where nothing could remove it.
tartisma: The aircraft met certification rules that didn't cover these droplets. When certification is incomplete, who notices first?
basliklar: Why American Eagle Flight 4184 Crashed
The Ice Nobody Designed For
sahneler: Holding in freezing rain, a turboprop suddenly rolled over.
It crashed into a field in Indiana, and sixty eight people were killed.
Ice had built up on its wings.
Its de-icing boots cracked off ice at the front.
But large droplets froze just behind them.
That ridge disturbed the airflow over the ailerons.
The controls snatched, and the plane rolled.
Icing certification later expanded to cover these droplets.

baslik: The Airliner That Suddenly Dove Twice on Its Own
sonuc: pitched down violently twice in cruise
tetik: spikes of false data from one air data unit
mekanizma: incorrect angle-of-attack spikes passed to flight control computers by a faulty ADIRU
ders: Airbus changed flight control software to reject data spikes
yanilgi: No turbulence hit the plane. The dives were commanded by the flight computers reacting to false data.
tartisma: The exact trigger for the data spikes was never found. Can you certify a fix for a fault you can't reproduce?
basliklar: Why Qantas Flight 72 Suddenly Dove
The False Data That Pushed an Airliner Down
soru: Fix a fault you can't reproduce?
sahneler: Cruising over Western Australia, an Airbus suddenly pitched down.
In seconds, unbelted passengers were thrown into the ceiling.
Then it happened again.
The pilots hadn't moved the controls.
One air data unit was sending short spikes of false data.
The flight computers read them as a stall and pushed the nose down.
The crew landed safely at a nearby air base.
Airbus then changed the software to reject spikes like these.

baslik: The Lightning Strike That Ignited a Fuel Tank
sonuc: exploded in flight near Elkton, Maryland
tetik: lightning striking the wing
mekanizma: lightning igniting fuel vapour in a reserve wing tank
ders: lightning protection standards for aircraft fuel systems were tightened
yanilgi: Aircraft are hit by lightning regularly. This one showed that fuel vents and tanks needed specific protection.
tartisma: The jet was holding near a storm while it waited. Should planes hold near thunderstorms at all?
basliklar: Why Pan Am Flight 214 Exploded
The Lightning Bolt That Changed Fuel Tank Design
sahneler: Holding near a thunderstorm, a Boeing 707 was struck by lightning.
A wing exploded, and all eighty one aboard were killed.
Planes are hit by lightning often and usually survive.
This strike reached fuel vapour in a reserve tank.
The vapour ignited and blew the tank apart.
The damaged wing separated.
Investigators studied how fuel vents and tanks handle lightning.
Lightning protection rules for fuel systems were tightened.

baslik: Britain's Giant Airship Crashed on Its First Big Voyage
sonuc: crashed and burned in France
tetik: loss of gas from damaged gasbags in bad weather
mekanizma: loss of lift from gasbag damage and a torn cover, causing a nose-down descent and hydrogen fire
ders: Britain abandoned its rigid airship programme
yanilgi: The flight wasn't doomed by one mistake. Rushed testing, leaking gasbags and bad weather combined on the first long trip.
tartisma: The voyage was timed to meet a political deadline. When should a schedule give way to testing?
basliklar: Why the R101 Airship Crashed
The Airship Rushed Into Service
sahneler: Britain's giant airship R101 crashed on a hillside in France.
Its hydrogen caught fire, and forty eight people were killed.
It was on its first long voyage, bound for India.
Testing had been rushed to meet a political deadline.
Its gasbags rubbed and leaked, losing lift.
In a storm, the nose dropped and it hit the ground.
Hydrogen turned the wreck into a fireball.
Britain then abandoned its rigid airship programme.

baslik: The Navy's Flying Aircraft Carrier Fell Into the Sea
sonuc: crashed into the Atlantic in a storm
tetik: a storm forcing the airship's tail into the water
mekanizma: severe storm downdraft and low flying altitude driving the tail into the sea
ders: the loss helped end the US Navy's rigid airship programme
yanilgi: Most men didn't die from the impact. They drowned or died of cold because there were no life jackets aboard.
tartisma: The airship carried almost no life jackets. How do obvious safety items get left behind?
basliklar: Why USS Akron Crashed
The Flying Aircraft Carrier With No Life Jackets
sahneler: The US Navy's giant airship Akron crashed into the Atlantic.
Seventy three of the seventy six men aboard died.
It had flown into a violent storm.
A downdraft pushed it lower and lower.
Its tail struck the water, and the structure broke up.
There were almost no life jackets aboard.
Most of the crew drowned in the cold sea.
The loss helped end the Navy's rigid airship programme.

baslik: A Software Glitch Shut Off the Engines Too Early
sonuc: went silent during landing on Mars
tetik: leg deployment jolts read as a touchdown signal
mekanizma: software treating spurious touchdown-sensor signals from leg deployment as landing, cutting the engines
ders: landing software is now tested with full end-to-end sensor behaviour
yanilgi: The lander most likely didn't crash from a hard terrain landing. Software probably shut its engines while it was still high above the surface.
tartisma: A test after a wiring fix was never rerun. How many retests are enough?
basliklar: Why Mars Polar Lander Went Silent
The False Touchdown That Killed a Mars Mission
sahneler: A NASA lander went silent as it descended to Mars.
It most likely crashed into the surface and was never heard from again.
The likely cause was a false signal.
When the legs unfolded, the jolt tripped the touchdown sensors.
The software remembered that signal.
High above the ground, it decided it had landed and cut the engines.
The lander fell the rest of the way.
Landing software is now tested end to end with real sensor behaviour.

baslik: A Sensor Installed Upside Down Crashed a NASA Capsule
sonuc: slammed into the Utah desert
tetik: accelerometers installed backwards
mekanizma: g-switch sensors mounted in the wrong orientation, so the parachutes never deployed
ders: orientation-critical parts now require independent verification
yanilgi: The parachutes didn't fail. They were never told to open, because the sensors were mounted backwards.
tartisma: Some solar wind samples were still recovered from the wreck. Is a partial success a failure?
basliklar: Why the Genesis Capsule Crashed
The Sensors Installed Upside Down
sahneler: A NASA capsule carrying pieces of the solar wind slammed into the Utah desert.
Its parachutes never opened, and it crashed at high speed.
The parachutes worked fine.
They were triggered by small acceleration sensors.
Those sensors had been installed backwards.
They never detected the capsule slowing down in the atmosphere.
Some samples were still recovered from the wreck.
Parts like these now need independent orientation checks.

baslik: Hubble's Mirror Was Ground Perfectly — to the Wrong Shape
sonuc: sent back blurry images after launch
tetik: a misassembled testing instrument used to shape the mirror
mekanizma: spherical aberration from a null corrector with a misplaced lens
ders: a corrective optics package was installed by astronauts in 1993
yanilgi: The mirror wasn't badly made. It was polished with extreme precision to the wrong shape.
tartisma: Other test instruments showed the error but were dismissed. When should one test override another?
basliklar: Why Hubble's First Images Were Blurry
The Perfect Mirror Ground to the Wrong Shape
sahneler: The Hubble Space Telescope was launched, and its first images came back blurry.
Suddenly, the billion-dollar observatory looked like a failure.
Its main mirror had been ground to the wrong shape.
It was polished with extreme precision against a faulty test tool.
One lens in that tool had been set in the wrong place.
Other tests hinted at the error but were dismissed.
Astronauts later installed corrective optics in orbit.
Hubble's images became some of the sharpest ever taken.

baslik: A Bent Pin Aborted a Crewed Launch Mid-Flight
sonuc: aborted during launch
tetik: a sensor pin bent during rocket assembly
mekanizma: a deformed separation sensor pin preventing a booster from separating cleanly
ders: assembly checks for separation sensors were tightened
yanilgi: The crew survived because the escape system worked, not because the failure was small.
tartisma: The pin was bent at the factory. How do you inspect damage that happens during assembly?
basliklar: Why Soyuz MS-10 Aborted
The Bent Pin That Stopped a Launch
sahneler: Two minutes into a crewed launch, a Soyuz rocket failed.
Suddenly, a booster struck the core stage and the rocket began to break up.
The escape system pulled the crew capsule away.
Both astronauts landed safely.
The cause was a bent pin on a separation sensor.
It had been damaged while the rocket was assembled.
The booster didn't separate cleanly.
Assembly checks for these sensors were tightened afterward.

baslik: A Decades-Old Engine Exploded Seconds After Launch
sonuc: exploded seconds after lift-off
tetik: a turbopump failure in a refurbished engine
mekanizma: failure in the liquid oxygen turbopump of a refurbished AJ26 engine
ders: Antares was re-engined with new RD-181 engines
yanilgi: The engines were not new designs. They were refurbished engines originally built for the Soviet Moon rocket.
tartisma: Using old engines saved money. How old is too old for rocket hardware?
basliklar: Why the Antares Orb-3 Rocket Exploded
The Old Engine That Failed on Launch
sahneler: Seconds after lift-off, a cargo rocket exploded over Virginia.
It fell back onto the launch pad in a fireball.
Nobody was aboard; it carried supplies for the space station.
Its engines were refurbished engines built decades earlier.
A turbopump in one of them failed.
With thrust lost, the rocket was destroyed.
The pad needed major repairs.
Antares was later rebuilt with new engines.

baslik: A Failed Steel Strut Broke Up a Falcon 9
sonuc: broke apart two minutes after launch
tetik: a steel strut holding a helium tank
mekanizma: failure of a strut securing a helium bottle in the second-stage oxygen tank
ders: SpaceX switched to struts with individual testing
yanilgi: No engine failed. A small part holding a tank inside the second stage gave way.
tartisma: The strut was a supplier part. How much should a company test parts it buys?
basliklar: Why SpaceX CRS-7 Broke Apart
The Strut That Failed Inside a Falcon 9
sahneler: Two minutes after launch, a Falcon 9 rocket broke apart.
The cargo bound for the space station was destroyed.
The cause was hidden inside the second stage.
A steel strut held a helium tank in place.
It failed below its rated strength.
The tank broke free and helium flooded out.
The pressure burst the stage.
SpaceX switched to struts tested one by one.

baslik: The Mars Lander That Thought It Was Underground
sonuc: crashed on Mars
tetik: a saturated rotation sensor for about one second
mekanizma: saturated inertial measurement unit leading software to compute a negative altitude
ders: ESA improved sensor-saturation handling and simulations for later landers
yanilgi: The parachute and thrusters worked. The software believed the lander was already below the surface.
tartisma: The saturation lasted around one second. How long should software trust a sensor stuck at its maximum?
basliklar: Why Schiaparelli Crashed on Mars
The Lander That Calculated It Was Underground
sahneler: Europe's Schiaparelli lander crashed on Mars.
It fell from high above the surface and was destroyed.
As its parachute opened, the lander spun hard.
A rotation sensor maxed out for about a second.
The software combined that bad value with other data.
It calculated an altitude below the ground.
So it released the parachute and fired its thrusters only briefly.
ESA improved how later landers handle saturated sensors.

baslik: A Weather Satellite Fell Over in the Factory
sonuc: fell off its stand during manufacturing
tetik: bolts removed from its holding fixture without anyone recording it
mekanizma: a turnover cart missing its bolts because procedures weren't followed
ders: NASA reinforced procedure checks for handling spacecraft
yanilgi: The satellite wasn't dropped by a crane. It slid off a cart whose bolts had been removed by another team.
tartisma: The step to verify the bolts was skipped because it seemed routine. Why do routine checks get skipped?
basliklar: How a Satellite Fell Over in the Factory
The Missing Bolts on a Weather Satellite
sahneler: A weather satellite being built for NOAA fell over in the factory.
It crashed to the floor and was badly damaged.
Workers were rotating it on a turnover cart.
The bolts that held it to the cart were missing.
Another team had removed them and not recorded it.
The step to check them was skipped.
The satellite was rebuilt and launched years later.
Handling procedures for spacecraft were reinforced.

baslik: Neil Armstrong's Spacecraft Spun Out of Control
sonuc: began spinning violently in orbit
tetik: a thruster stuck on after an electrical short
mekanizma: a stuck-open orbital attitude thruster causing a rapidly increasing spin
ders: thruster circuits were changed so a single fault could be isolated
zincir: RE-ENTRY THRUSTERS USED TO STOP IT
yanilgi: The spin wasn't caused by the target vehicle. It came from a thruster on Gemini itself.
tartisma: Using the re-entry thrusters forced the mission to end early. Is ending a mission early a failure?
basliklar: Why Gemini 8 Spun Out of Control
The Stuck Thruster Armstrong Had to Stop
sahneler: In orbit, Neil Armstrong's spacecraft began spinning out of control.
Suddenly, it rolled faster and faster, close to making the crew black out.
They had just docked with a target vehicle.
One of Gemini's own thrusters was stuck on.
Undocking only made the spin faster.
Armstrong used the re-entry thrusters to stop it.
The mission had to end early.
Thruster circuits were redesigned to isolate a single fault.

baslik: Apollo 12 Was Struck by Lightning Twice During Launch
sonuc: was hit by lightning during launch
tetik: the rocket and its exhaust plume triggering lightning in clouds
mekanizma: vehicle-triggered lightning knocking fuel cells offline and scrambling telemetry
ders: launch rules now forbid launching through clouds that can trigger lightning
yanilgi: There was no active thunderstorm overhead. The rocket itself triggered the lightning.
tartisma: One engineer remembered an obscure switch that saved the mission. How do you capture knowledge like that?
basliklar: How Apollo 12 Survived Two Lightning Strikes
The Rocket That Triggered Its Own Lightning
sahneler: Seconds after lift-off, Apollo 12 was struck by lightning.
Seconds later it was hit again, and warnings flooded the cabin.
The rocket itself had triggered the lightning in the clouds.
Fuel cells dropped offline and the data went haywire.
An engineer on the ground recalled an obscure switch setting.
Flipping it restored the data.
The mission went on to land on the Moon.
Launch rules now forbid flying through clouds like these.

baslik: A Clock Set Wrong Sent Starliner Into the Wrong Orbit
sonuc: failed to reach the space station
tetik: a mission timer set from the wrong moment
mekanizma: the spacecraft pulling its elapsed-time clock from the rocket at the wrong point
ders: Boeing reworked its software testing before flying again
yanilgi: The engines worked. The spacecraft simply believed it was at a different point in the mission.
tartisma: End-to-end tests were split into chunks. Is a test that stops halfway a test at all?
basliklar: Why Starliner Missed the Space Station
The Clock That Was Set Wrong
sahneler: Boeing's uncrewed Starliner reached space but couldn't get to the station.
Suddenly, it began burning fuel as if it were far later in the mission.
Its mission clock was wrong.
It had read the time from the rocket at the wrong moment.
The spacecraft used too much fuel to reach its target.
The docking had to be cancelled.
Tests had not run the full mission end to end.
Boeing reworked its software testing before flying again.

baslik: A Satellite Spun Itself to Pieces Weeks After Launch
sonuc: broke apart in orbit
tetik: an attitude error followed by a thruster command with wrong parameters
mekanizma: spin-up from faulty attitude estimation, then thrusters firing in the wrong direction
ders: JAXA tightened review of uploaded commands and parameters
yanilgi: No debris hit it. The satellite's own control system spun it faster until parts broke off.
tartisma: A wrong parameter file had been uploaded without full checks. Who double-checks the numbers?
basliklar: Why the Hitomi Satellite Broke Apart
The Wrong Parameters That Spun a Satellite
sahneler: A new Japanese X-ray satellite broke apart weeks after launch.
It spun faster and faster until its solar panels were destroyed.
It began with a glitch in estimating its orientation.
The satellite thought it was rotating when it wasn't.
Its correction added real spin instead.
Then thrusters fired using wrongly set parameters.
That made the spin worse, and the structure failed.
JAXA tightened checks on uploaded commands and settings.

baslik: The Soviet Moon Rocket That Failed Every Launch
sonuc: failed in all four launch attempts
tetik: thirty first-stage engines that were never tested together
mekanizma: complex clustered engines and control system without full ground testing of the first stage
ders: the Soviet crewed lunar programme was cancelled
yanilgi: It wasn't one bad launch. All four flights failed, one of them destroying its own launch pad.
tartisma: Testing the whole first stage on the ground was skipped to save time and money. Is testing ever optional?
basliklar: Why the N1 Moon Rocket Failed
Thirty Engines That Were Never Tested Together
sahneler: The Soviet Moon rocket N1 failed on every launch.
One exploded just after lift-off and destroyed its own launch pad.
Its first stage used thirty engines.
They were never fired together on the ground before flight.
When one failed, problems cascaded through the cluster.
The control system shut down engines it shouldn't have.
After four failures, the programme stopped.
The Soviet crewed lunar landing was cancelled.
